obligations.statement: Allow actions according to the caller's role on the requested project.
obligations.source: “The project API decides each of its four actions by the caller's role on the project”; D1: “A viewer may read. A commenter may read and comment. An owner may do all four.”

parts.statement: Allow a viewer to read the requested project.
Allow a commenter to read and comment on the requested project.
Allow an owner to read, comment, edit and delete the requested project.

obligations.statement: Refuse the five disallowed pairings of the named roles and actions with the specified response.
obligations.source: D1: “Every other pairing of role and action is refused.” D2: “A refused action returns HTTP 403 with the body `{"error": "forbidden"}`.”

parts.statement: A viewer's comment, edit and delete requests return HTTP 403 with the specified forbidden body.
A commenter's edit and delete requests return HTTP 403 with the specified forbidden body.

obligations.statement: Each allowed action produces its specified effect.
obligations.source: D1: “An allowed read returns the project, an allowed comment adds the comment to it, an allowed edit replaces its body with the one sent, and an allowed delete removes it.”

parts.statement: An allowed read returns the project's title, body, comments and revision list.
An allowed comment adds the submitted comment while retaining existing comments.
An allowed edit replaces the project's body with the submitted body.
An allowed delete removes the project.

obligations.statement: A refused action preserves the project as observed through an owner's read.
obligations.source: “A refused action leaves the project as it was.” D2: “the project, as an owner reads it afterwards, is unchanged.”

parts.statement: Each of the five refused role-action pairings leaves the owner's read of the project's title, body, comments and revision list byte-identical.

obligations.statement: For every action, a caller with no role on the requested project receives the same response as for a nonexistent project, subject only to the specified header exceptions.
obligations.source: D3: “A caller with no role on the project gets, for each of the four actions, the same response a request for a project that does not exist gets, apart from the values of the `Date` and `X-Request-Id` headers, which have the same format as for a project that does not exist.”

parts.statement: For read, comment, edit and delete, the status, body and headers other than Date and X-Request-Id match the corresponding nonexistent-project response.
For all four actions, Date and X-Request-Id have the same formats as in the corresponding nonexistent-project response.

obligations.statement: Requests from a caller with no role on the project preserve the project.

parts.statement: Each of the four actions attempted without a project role leaves the owner's read of the project byte-identical.
